title: Opera, the Philharmonic Society and boatmen in the balconies
summary: Opera was the main classical endeavor; the only permanent resident opera company, with boatmen filling the galleries.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: They, uh, had an amateur society before the Civil War called the Philharmonic Society that played, uh, attempted to play, uh, symphonic pieces. And the opera orchestra would play symphonic pieces. They gave a great many smaller concerts, which helped the opera musicians to pay their expenses and, uh, make a better salary. But the chief classical endeavor was far and away opera, no question about it. Mm-hmm. In fact, at one time in 1837, I believe it was, you could go out on a Friday night here and choose from among three operas. And then the same on Saturday night, choose from among three operas, which is remarkable in a city which was still fairly small by today's standards.
Mm-hmm. But, uh, well in 1837 Atlanta was nothing. Hardly on the map. Yeah. Uh, so you, you had so much like that. But Charleston was an old city and…

Yes, and has had some, uh, history and they had, of course, the St. Cecilia Society and Charleston and a choral history. Uh, but nothing like a permanent resident opera company. This was the only permanent resident opera company in the United States in those days. Mm-hmm. In fact, uh, you might say, uh, possibly the only, uh, really long-term continuous one until the, uh, advent of, uh, post-Civil War Chicago opera, Metropolitan Opera and San Francisco opera. This city was, uh, in this business from, well really almost from 1800 on. In fact, the first, uh, theater was opened in 1792 and there were operas performed in the 1790s. They couldn't have been, the production couldn't have been much, but they were trying and they were on the track. After 1819, then they had imported good-sized orchestras from mainly France, but Italy also and Germany. Uh, that is musicians from these countries making up the orchestra. Mm-hmm. All of them bringing with them a good deal of their own classical tradition and ways and approaches. But, of course, also pouring in here all the time down the Mississippi River was every bit of, uh, country and folk music that the United States had. Coming in with boatmen and all. And, uh, these boatmen, uh, for lack of other amusements, went to the opera. Really?

They, they'd fill the balconies and, uh, much to the annoyance of a lot of the, uh, study customers because they'd chop on apples and crack nuts and, uh, all sorts of things like that. You see, there were, after the St. Charles Theater opened, well, even earlier, uh, the first American theater to be built specifically for that purpose was opened in 1823 and that was a theater on Camp Street. Sometimes called the American theater, sometimes called the Camp Street Theater. And, uh, it used, uh, mounted operas. Now, it was never as good as the, uh, Orleans Theater, which was the French, uh, opera theater. But it did mount operas and, uh, some of them were successful. And, uh, even such a thing as, uh, the Freischutz, in the somewhat truncated version, was first played in New Orleans in the Camp Street Theater. But then, uh, in the 1830s, the St. Charles Theater, I think the first opening was 1835, and then there was a fire and it was rebuilt and opened again, but the St. Charles Street Theater, the St. Charles Theater was open. They had a huge orchestra, maybe, maybe 35 pieces or so, and were definitely out to rival the French, the Orleans Theater, where the French opera was. And to do this, they imported from Havana a very fine Italian opera troupe, a singing Italian opera. And, uh, in their first seasons, uh, uh, used, uh, represented such operas as, uh, Norma and, uh, uh, composers like, uh, along with Bellini, like, uh, well, Rossini had been played before, but they did more of Rossini. And, uh, the Italian opera as it existed at the time, so that you had the—what was called the French Opera—and even this is a misnomer— the French Opera House by no means confined itself to the French composed operas. operas. They used every opera there was, merely changing the lyrics to French, and thus Der Freischütz became Robin de Bois in the French theater.
